instagram_caption:
Lose $100 million of other people's money. Still get paid $20 million.

It's called "2 and 20". Many hedge funds charge about 2% of your money every year, plus about 20% of the profits (the SEC's Investor.gov says typical fees are 1-2% of assets and 15-20% of profits). On a $1 billion fund, 2% is $20 million a year. A year up 20% adds another $40 million in profit fees. A year down 10% loses investors $100 million, and the 2% is still about $20 million. Simplified example: real fees vary by fund.

Would you pay 2% a year, win or lose?

Source: SEC Investor.gov (fetched Nov 18, 2026). Maths in Python. Not financial advice.
